column3: It repeats the closing test of who is in manifest error, while grounding it in trust in the Merciful.
Its imposed surah and clear signs parallel the Quran obligation and guidance-bearing revelation in the focus.
The divinely fixed alms allocation shares the language of obligation but not the Quranic commission or return.
Moses says almost the same formula: his Lord knows who brought guidance and whose final outcome will prevail.
The immediately following verse calls the Book bestowed on the Prophet a mercy, directly continuing the focus's Quranic address.
God's beginning and restoring provides a broad return motif but does not specify the promised destination.
The return of Joseph's father's sight and his claim of divine knowledge are a distant narrative echo.
God promises to return Moses and make him a messenger, a direct earlier pattern of assured return in the same surah.
Its prescribed marital due is a different legal use of obligation, without the focus's commission or return.
It closely parallels the focus's contrast: the Lord knows who strays from His way and who is guided.
Its alternative between guidance and manifest error closely matches the focus's closing discernment.
Being turned back to disbelief is a moral reversal, not the promised return of the bearer of the Quran.
It repeats the Lord's knowledge of those astray from His path and of the guided.
The nearby command to call to the Lord after revelation extends the focus's commission into faithful response.
Warning against being turned back by disbelievers only loosely contrasts with the focus's promised return.
It directly addresses the Quran sent down upon the Prophet, though it does not state the return.
Moses's preservation as a child supplies earlier same-surah context for the return and mission later promised in 28:7.
The tribal name Ad only shares an Arabic root incidentally and adds no return or guidance connection.
The statement that the Lord knows human deeds shares the opening knowledge formula but not its guidance contrast.
Mutual non-liability for deeds does not develop the imposed Quran, return, or guidance-error contrast.
The deniers' question about being returned introduces resurrection return, though in a different argumentative setting.
Its confession of manifest error repeats the focus's exact error description, without its guidance half.
The nearby conclusion that all return to God supplies the ultimate horizon for the promised maad.
It explicitly states that return is to God and contrasts that final return with futile calls.
The quick return of a glance is a literal but unrelated use of return language.
God returns Moses to his mother so that His promise becomes known as true, a direct same-surah return pattern.
The punishment that cannot be turned back is a different negative use of the return root.
It explicitly names the Quran's sending down, supporting the focus's Quranic commission without its promised return.
It joins increased guidance to a better final return, closely resonating with both major poles of the focus.
The command to worship sincerely ends by saying people return as they began, giving a broad return parallel.
The messenger teaches the Book and wisdom to people formerly in manifest error, echoing revelation, guidance, and error.
The delivery of Solomon's letter has no material connection to the Quranic commission or promised return.
It declares that all will be returned to the Knower of unseen and seen, directly clarifying final return.
It contrasts retreat after divine guidance with answering the call to guidance, closely sharpening the focus's distinction.
Listening attentively is not a distinct connection to the focus's return or guidance formula.
The obligation of pilgrimage is a separate prescribed duty and only broadly resembles the imposed Quran.
The messenger is sent with guidance and true religion, supporting the focus's identification of the one who brings guidance.
The command to follow a divinely given way rather than ignorant desires reinforces the focus's guidance versus error contrast.
Being returned to feeble old age is a different temporal return, not the appointed maad.
The messenger is sent with guidance and true religion, supporting the focus's identification of the one who brings guidance.
Misguidance through following desire is relevant to error, but does not closely parallel the focus's formula.
The warning not to turn back after entering the holy land uses reversal language in a separate Moses episode.
The messenger's mission with guidance and true religion gives a close thematic counterpart to bringing guidance.
God finding and guiding the Prophet offers a concise positive counterpart to manifest error.
The restoration of power after defeat is a historical return, not the appointed return of the Quran's bearer.
The Quran is revealed to the Prophet as a warning, directly supporting the focus's Quranic mission.
Clear signs and divine guidance to a straight path echo the focus's contrast between guidance and manifest error.
God sending the disbelievers back frustrated is a different event-level use of return language.
Trading guidance for error states the same moral opposition, though without the focus's return promise.
The command to throw first does not bear on return, Quranic commission, or guidance.
Returning horses to Solomon is an unrelated literal return.
It explicitly calls the Quran revelation to the Prophet, providing a direct commission-related parallel.
Divine light and guidance are a broad metaphorical counterpart, not a specific return or formula link.
The wish to turn believers back to disbelief is a different reversal from the promised return in the focus.
It contrasts personal error with being guided through what the Lord reveals, closely linking revelation, guidance, and error.
Sending a letter and awaiting a reply does not develop the focus's return or guidance claim.
The word for an aged cow is only an incidental root overlap with obligation.
The brothers call their father in manifest error, repeating the exact description but in a different narrative judgment.
It says people will be returned to the Knower of unseen and seen for disclosure of deeds.
Returning oaths is a legal procedure unrelated to the focus's promised return.
It calls the Quran guidance for people and marks its signs of guidance, directly supporting that element of the focus.
It states that people will be returned to the Knower of unseen and seen, though in a hypocrites context.
A husband's right to take back a divorced wife is a distinct legal return.
The believer from Pharaoh's family invokes clear signs and denies guidance to extravagant liars, a limited Moses-era echo.
Acceptance of repentance and alms does not materially illuminate the commission, return, or error formula.
The wrongdoer is returned to his Lord for further punishment, giving a direct final-return pattern in a different context.
God's command arrives and judgment is settled, broadly resonating with an appointed divine outcome.
The verse concerns excuses and sealed hearts, without a meaningful focus connection.
A prescribed marital payment is another legal use of obligation but not the Quranic imposition.
God's prescribed expiation for oaths is a separate legal obligation with no return or guidance link.
Casting Joseph away is not the promised return or the focus's guidance-error contrast.
Turning someone from religion and apostasy concern moral reversal, only distantly related to return language.
God's ordained matter for the Prophet supports the focus's divinely imposed commission, though the subject differs.
Return to great punishment is a final-return motif but lacks the focus's positive promise or guidance contrast.
All are returned to God, the true Master and Judge, directly framing the ultimate meaning of maad.
The warning about returning to usury does not clarify the focus's promise of return.
The harmful mosque narrative has no material connection to the focus's themes.
Those facing fulfillment wish to be returned to act otherwise, a direct but negative final-return parallel.
Truth's arrival and falsehood's inability to begin or return loosely echo the focus's arrival and return vocabulary.
Awaiting the envoys' return is a narrative detail unrelated to the promised maad.
Wrongdoers who see punishment ask whether any route of return remains, directly contrasting the focus's assured return.
Jesus comes with clear signs and the disbelievers call them manifest magic, a limited sign-and-error echo.
Alms purification and prayer do not add to the focus's commission, return, or guidance distinction.
What was prescribed concerning spouses is a separate legal prescription, not the imposed Quran.
Rejecting messengers and doubting their call gives general revelation-rejection context, but not the focus's return claim.
The coming of death under divine guardianship does not itself express return or guidance.
The return of merchandise enables another journey but is not materially connected to the focus.
The condemned ask to be brought out and promise not to return to wrongdoing, a distant return contrast.
Souls are returned to God, their true Master, while their false claims vanish, closely matching final return and error exposure.
Return to the earth followed by emergence supplies a broad bodily cycle of return, not the focus's appointed destination.
God's encompassing knowledge of creation does not specifically develop the focus's return or guidance formula.
Written debts with a fixed term offer only a remote parallel to an imposed obligation and appointed time.
Satan's retreat from battle does not illuminate the focus's promised return.
Reaching an appointed term and then the Fire gives a broad destination motif, but not the focus's return promise.
Completing nursing and its obligations provide only a remote completion-of-duty parallel.
The mention of two additional gardens has no connection to the focus's themes.
Broken promises leading to hypocrisy do not develop the promised return or guidance contrast.
Entering a blazing fire does not materially connect to the focus.
God's call to Abraham alone provides no distinct return, Quran, or guidance link.
It commands response to the Lord before an irreversible day arrives, strongly framing the gravity of final return.
Pharaoh and his chiefs wrongly suppose that they will not be returned to God, directly opposing the focus's assured return.
It challenges opponents to produce a divine book more guiding than the two already given, directly joining Book and guidance.
It calls the follower of desire without divine guidance more astray, closely matching the focus's guidance versus manifest error contrast.
God says He has conveyed the Word to them for remembrance, extending the immediate Quranic-revelation context.
It distinguishes human inability to guide from God's knowledge of the truly guided, directly sharpening the focus's final claim.
The objection that following guidance will bring expulsion gives immediate-surah resistance context for the focus's guidance claim.
The Quran is introduced as a Book containing guidance, a foundational parallel to the imposed Quran and its guidance claim.
God guides those who seek His pleasure through the revealed message to paths of peace and a straight path.
The revelation from the Lord is described as guidance and mercy, directly supporting the Quranic guidance in the focus.
It explicitly states that this Quran guides to what is most upright, directly explaining the focus's Quran and guidance pairing.
Whoever follows guidance sent from God will neither go astray nor suffer, tightly reversing the focus's manifest-error pole.
Every soul tastes death and then returns to God, a clear general statement of the promised final return.
It rejects the claim that people were created aimlessly and would not be returned to God, directly paralleling the focus's return assertion.
God originates creation, repeats it, and then people return to Him, explicitly combining restoration and final return.
After death, people are returned to their Lord, providing a direct final-return formulation.
The speaker worships the Creator to whom all will be returned, supplying a direct devotional counterpart to maad.
It concludes that all things return to God, a concise direct statement of the final return.
God guides by the Quranic message whom He wills, directly connecting the Book to divine guidance.
The Quran is called guidance and healing for believers, directly supporting the focus's Quran-guidance connection.
The revealed Spirit is made a light by which God guides, and the Prophet guides to a straight path.
The Prophet is commanded to hold fast to what has been revealed because he is on a straight path.
The jinn describe the Book sent after Moses as confirming truth and guiding to truth and a straight path.
God increases those already guided in guidance, a direct positive development of the focus's guidance category.
